newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies close up on strong cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies close up on strong cash.

text.p: The continued strong tone to cash markets kept CME hog futures strong at the close after a new high in February. Pork bellies ran up from early losses to end higher following cash strength.

February hog futures posted a new high of 79.200 cents and December came within 0.025 cent of its high set Friday before futures slipped to close 0.425 cent higher to unchanged. February paced the gain on rolling and December ended up 0.225 at 59.375 cents.
"Cash (hog) markets are running stronger than expected," one trader said. Only cash hams were showing some seasonal weakness.

The firm product market was keeping packer interest for hogs strong. Packers were being forced to raise bids for hogs as producers continued to retain gilts for breeding and the total hog supply seems to be below previous projections, traders said.
However, the gain in December was limited by funds rolling long positions into February. December is now the spot month and open interest is still very large, they said.

R.J. O'Brien notably bought December while Refco, Prudential Securities and Dean Witter bought February. Rand Financials sold on the early advance. R.J. O'Brien also spread long February/short June with Rosenthal Collins on the other side, pit sources said.
In hog options, volatility was down in December based on the time decay. Stone Traders sold April 70 puts and 78 calls. Locals bought 80 to 84 February calls, pit sources added.
Pork belly futures rallied from early profit-taking losses as prices held technical support above a gap in the charts, traders said.

Local short-covering and commercial buying interest then pushed prices up for net gains late, partly influenced by the strong tone to cash bellies, lighter than expected pace of hog slaughter and small storage stocks. Cash belly prices ranged up to $74 per cwt at noon, the highest price level since early October, they said.

Dean Witter, LFG and Paine Webber bought on the advance. Prudential Securities sold early, pit sources said. Pork bellies closed 0.025 to 1.100 cent higher with February up 0.275 at 81.375 cents. (Jerry Bieszk 312-408-8725)
